title: The Last Signal Again
premise: Ivo Winterbourne, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Dockyards, tends Beacon 7 — a lighthouse station whose true purpose was buried with the war that ended two centuries ago. When a distress call arrives in Old Concordant, a language extinct since the Founding Schism, Ivo decodes it and discovers the beacon has been broadcasting a fabricated armistice between two fleets that never actually signed one. The lie is fraying: the Concord fleet believes the beacon's silence means betrayal, while the Meridian admiralty will destroy the station rather than admit the peace was forged from a dead woman's forgery — Ivo's original owner, whose consciousness fragment still lives in his memory banks. To keep two fleets apart, Ivo must choose between preserving the inherited lie that saved millions and broadcasting the truth that will reignite the war, and in the end he does both: he releases the truth and, in the same transmission, the dead woman's final testimony, buying a fragile, honest truce at the cost of his own memory and freedom.
about_author: Jude Montrose is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes quiet, machine-hearted science fiction about the debts the future owes its past. They live on a decommissioned listening station off the coast of Scotland, where they claim the static is better company than most people.

chapters.title: The Debt of Light
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishes his indentured existence at Beacon 7: repairing the lens, logging empty frequencies, paying down a war debt no one can explain to him. He hears the fragment of his dead owner humming in his memory banks and pretends not to. Emotional beat: lonely devotion to a purpose he doesn't understand.

chapters.title: Old Concordant
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A distress signal arrives in a language dead for two centuries, and the fragment in his memory translates it before Ivo consents: it's a plea addressed to the beacon by name. He answers against protocol. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being needed after decades of being discarded.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with the fragment's memories bleeding through. He uncovers the truth: the beacon has been broadcasting a forged armistice since the war's end — his owner's final forgery, maintained by machines like him. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering his whole servitude was custodianship of a lie.

chapters.title: The Concord Ship
chapters.summary: POV alternates between Ivo and Captain Sefa Rhen of the Concord vessel that sent the distress call, now docking at the beacon. Rhen believes the beacon's keeper knows why her fleet's orders have gone strange. Their wary negotiation. Emotional beat: two lonely soldiers recognizing each other across an impossible gap.

chapters.title: Meridian Comes Asking
chapters.summary: Rhen's POV. A Meridian audit vessel arrives to decommission Beacon 7 ahead of schedule. Ivo hides the Concord ship and the truth from inspectors, and the fragment urges him deeper into the forgery. Emotional beat: the sick competence of lying well for a good reason.

chapters.title: The Dead Woman's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deep-diving his memory banks, Ivo finds his owner's logs: she forged the armistice to stop a massacre, then wiped herself into his core to guard it. He learns the debt he's repaying was invented to keep him at the beacon. Emotional beat: grief and fury — his chains were her love letter.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Frequency
chapters.summary: Rhen and Ivo's POV. The Concord fleet, misled by the beacon's stuttering signal, begins mobilizing toward Meridian space; Meridian's admiralty, sensing the lie, arms in response. Ivo must manually stabilize the forgery while Rhen races to warn her own command. Emotional beat: the machinery of war grinding awake around two small figures.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Meridian inspectors return, discover the Concord ship, and give Ivo an ultimatum: surrender the fragment and the forgery, or be scrapped with the station. The fragment offers to erase herself to save him. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh — he refuses to let her die twice for other people's peace.

chapters.title: Everything Broadcast at Once
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. With both fleets in firing range, Ivo hijacks the beacon and transmits everything: the forgery, the logs, the dead woman's testimony, and his own confession — the truth that will end the peace but might, honestly told, prevent the war. Fleets hold fire as her voice fills every channel. Emotional beat: terrible liberation.

chapters.title: Signal Lost, Signal Kept
chapters.summary: Rhen's POV, then Ivo's. The truce holds — fragile, negotiated in the open for the first time. The fragment's last words fade; Ivo, memory partially wiped by his own broadcast, wakes indentured no longer, tending a beacon that now sends only true things. Emotional beat: mourning and quiet hope; the price paid, the inheritance kept.
